attrib.value: Forestry Revocation and National Park Reservation Act 1996

block.txt: An Act to revoke the dedication of certain lands as State forest (including national forest) and the status of certain lands as flora reserve; to reserve lands as, or as parts of, national parks and to dedicate lands as, or as parts of, nature reserves; and for other purposes.
This Act is the Forestry Revocation and National Park Reservation Act 1996.
This Act commences on 1 January 1997.

heading.b: Revocation of status of certain lands as flora reserve

block.txt: The notices specified in Schedule 1, setting apart areas of State forest as flora reserves, are revoked but only to the extent to which they relate to flora reserves or parts of flora reserves situated within State forests whose dedication is revoked by this Act.

Any other notice under section 25A of the Forestry Act 1916 that sets apart, as flora reserve, the whole or any portion of a State forest whose dedication is revoked by this Act is, to the extent to which the notice relates to flora reserve situated within such State forest, also revoked.

heading.b: Revocation of dedication of certain lands as State forest

block.txt: The dedication as State forest of the lands described in Schedule 2 is revoked.

The lands described in Part 26 of Schedule 2 are dedicated as part of Nadgee Nature Reserve.

heading.b: Revocation of reservation, and reservation, of other lands as national park

block.txt: The reservation of land as Barrington Tops National Park is, to the extent that that reservation applies to the land described in Part 1 of Schedule 3, revoked. The land described in that Part is reserved as part of Mount Royal National Park.

The reservation of land as Werrikimbe National Park is, to the extent that that reservation applies to the land described in Part 2 of Schedule 3, revoked. The land described in that Part is reserved as part of Oxley Wild Rivers National Park.

heading.b: Alteration of names of certain national parks

block.txt: The name of each of the following national parks is altered to South East Forest National Park with the intention that, on the commencement of this Act, each of the parks becomes part of that Park:
Bemboka National Park
Coolangubra National Park
Genoa National Park
Tantawangalo National Park
Yowaka National Park.

heading.b: Special provision as to access roads

block.txt: In this section:
access roads means the roads, tracks, trails and other means of access referred to in subsection (2) (a)–(o).
Environment Minister means the Minister administering the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.
private land holding means land held:
by an owner within the meaning of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974, or
as a holding within the meaning of the Crown Land Management Act 2016.

roads used, immediately before the commencement of this Act, for access to private land holdings within the lands referred to in this section,
roads through the lands referred to in this section to State forests or private land holdings that adjoin or are in the vicinity of the lands.

The access roads to which this section applies are not, on the commencement of this Act, reserved as, or as part of, a national park by the operation of section 5 or dedicated as, or as part of, a nature reserve by the operation of section 6 but vest in the Environment Minister on behalf of the Crown for the purposes of Part 11 of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 for an estate in fee simple, freed and discharged from:
all trusts, obligations, estates, interests, rights of way or other easements, and
any dedication, reservation, Crown grant or vesting to which the lands were subject, and any such dedication, reservation, grant or vesting is revoked by the operation of this section.
The access roads may continue, subject to this section, to be used for the purposes for which they were used immediately before the commencement of this Act.

Within 6 months after the commencement of this Act (or within such further period as the Environment Minister may, by notice published in the Gazette, notify before the expiration of that period) the Environment Minister must, by one or more orders published in the Gazette, declare which of the access roads to which this section applies:
are excluded from reservation as part of a national park or dedication as part of a nature reserve, or
are not so excluded and are reserved as part of the national park or dedicated as part of the nature reserve in which they are situated.
An order under this subsection may be published only with the concurrence of the Minister administering the Forestry Act 1916.
On the publication of an order under subsection (5):

the access roads that are referred to in the order as excluded from reservation as part of a national park or dedication as part of a nature reserve remain vested in the Environment Minister for the purposes of Part 11 of the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 and may, subject to this section, continue to be used for the purposes for which they were used immediately before the commencement of this Act, and
the access roads that are not so excluded are reserved as part of the national park or dedicated as part of the nature reserve within which they are situated.

Nothing in this section affects the exercise of any power, authority, duty or function by the Environment Minister or any other person under and in accordance with the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974 in relation to any access road to which this section applies.
While a private land holding is in private ownership, nothing in this section authorises the Environment Minister to close any access road that comprises the only means of access to the land holding.
This section has effect despite the provisions of the Forestry Act 1916.

any dedication, reservation, Crown grant or vesting to which the lands were subject, and any such dedication, reservation, grant or vesting is revoked by the operation of this section.

heading.b: Exclusion of freehold and certain leasehold interests

block.txt: Despite any other provision of this Act, no land that a person holds:
for an estate in fee simple, or
under a continued perpetual lease, a continued special lease or a continued term lease within the meaning of Schedule 1 to the Crown Land Management Act 2016,
is, by the operation of this Act, reserved as, or as part of, a national park or dedicated as, or as part of, a nature reserve.
Schedule 4 has effect.

In this Schedule:
Forestry Act means the Forestry Act 1916.
NPW Act means the National Parks and Wildlife Act 1974.

heading.b: Revocation of dedication of State forest

block.txt: Section 4 has effect despite the provisions of the Forestry Act.

heading.b: Reservation of lands as national parks

block.txt: The lands reserved as national parks by section 5 (2)–(10) are, for the purposes of the NPW Act, taken to have been so reserved by proclamation made under section 33 (2) of that Act.

The lands reserved as parts of national parks by sections 5 (11)–(25), 7 and 9 (6) (b) are, for the purposes of the NPW Act, taken to have been so reserved by proclamation made under section 33 (3) of that Act.

A reference in the NPW Act to the publication of a proclamation under section 33 (2) or (3) of that Act is, in relation to a reservation referred to in section 5, 7 or 9, taken to be a reference to the enactment of this Act.
Section 35 of the NPW Act does not apply to a reservation of land as, or as part of, a national park that is effected by this Act.
A name assigned to a national park by section 5 (2)–(10) is taken to have been assigned to that park by a proclamation referred to in section 36 (a) of the NPW Act.
The alteration of the name of a national park by section 8 is taken to have been made by a proclamation referred to in section 36 (b) of the NPW Act.

heading.b: Dedication of lands as nature reserve

block.txt: The lands dedicated as a nature reserve by section 6 (2) are, for the purposes of the NPW Act, taken to have been so dedicated by proclamation made under section 49 (1) of that Act.

The lands dedicated as part of a nature reserve by section 6 (3) or 9 (6) (b) are, for the purposes of the NPW Act, taken to have been so dedicated by proclamation made under section 49 (2) of that Act.

A reference in the NPW Act, being a reference to, or a reference to be construed as a reference to, the publication of a proclamation under section 49 (1) or (2) of that Act is, in relation to a dedication referred to in section 6 or 9, taken to be a reference to the enactment of this Act.
Section 35 of the NPW Act as applied to nature reserves by section 58 (b) of that Act does not apply to a dedication of land as, or as part of, a nature reserve that is effected by this Act.
A name assigned to a nature reserve by section 6 (2) is taken to have been assigned to that reserve by a proclamation referred to in section 51 (a) of the NPW Act.
Section 42 (2) of the NPW Act applies to and in respect of a lease under the Forestry Act, being a lease:
affecting any of the lands described in Schedule 2, and
current and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act,
in the same way as it applies to a licence or permit under the Forestry Act, affecting lands within a national park.

heading.b: Administration of existing leases and similar interests

block.txt: In this clause, existing interest means a lease, licence, permit or occupancy current and in force immediately before the commencement of this Act.
The administration of matters relating to existing interests, to the extent that those interests affect any of the lands described in Schedule 2, is vested in the Minister administering the NPW Act.
For the purposes of subclause (2), the Minister administering the NPW Act has:
in respect of existing interests under the Forestry Act—the powers of the Minister administering that Act, and
in respect of existing interests under the Crown Land Management Act 2016—the powers of the Minister administering that Act.
A revocation effected by this Act does not affect anything done or omitted to be done before the commencement of this Act.
